description: Unlimited OCR Works: Welcome the Era of One-shot Long-horizon Parsing.

detail.readme:
Unlimited OCR Works

Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing.

## Release - [2026/11/02] 📄 The paper of **Unlimited OCR 2** is now available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.39308). - [2026/10/28] Thanks to the [ms-swift community](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) for supporting training of **Unlimited OCR 2**. - [2026/10/27] 📊 We release [**MarathonDocBench**](https://huggingface.co/datasets/baidu/MarathonDocBench), a new benchmark for ultra-long document parsing. - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to the [ModelScope community](https://github.com/modelscope) for their support. Our model is now available at [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/PaddlePaddle/Unlimited-OCR-2). - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to the Baidu Cloud team for their support. Our model is now available on [Baidu Cloud](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/OCR/s/fmr1p39gb). - [2026/10/27] 🤝 Thanks to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for creating a new demo for us. Try it at [Unlimited-OCR-2](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2). - [2026/10/27] 🚀 We release [**Unlimited OCR 2**](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR), achieving unlimited-horizon parsing with SR-SWA. - [2026/07/21] 🤝 Thanks to the [ms-swift community](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift) for their support, our model now supports training with [ms-swift](https://github.com/modelscope/ms-swift). - [2026/07/03] 🤝 Thanks to the Baidu Cloud team for their support. Our model is now available on [Baidu Cloud](https://cloud.baidu.com/doc/OCR/s/fmr1p39gb). - [2026/06/28] 🤝 Thanks to the [vLLM community](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm) and [Tianyu Guo](https://github.com/gty111) for their support, our model now supports vLLM inference. - [2026/06/24] 🤝 Thanks to [AK](https://x.com/_akhaliq) for creating a demo for us. It is now available at [Hugging Face Spaces](https://huggingface.co/spaces/baidu/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/23] 📄 Our paper is now available on [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.23050). - [2026/06/23] 🤝 Thanks to the [ModelScope community](https://github.com/modelscope) for their support. Our model is now available at [ModelScope](https://modelscope.cn/models/PaddlePaddle/Unlimited-OCR). - [2026/06/22] 🚀 We present [Unlimited-OCR](https://github.com/baidu/Unlimited-OCR/tree/UnlimitedOCR1.0), aiming to push [Deepseek-OCR](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-OCR) one step further. ## What's New in 2 * Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA): Compresses text-visual attention interactions from ultra-long sequences down to a fixed-size set of working references (e.g., 512 tokens). This bounds computational complexity, keeping per-step decoding latency and memory footprint nearly constant regardless of document length. * From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing: Powered by SR-SWA, Unlimited-OCR 2 achieves true, unbounded document parsing within a finite context window—effectively eliminating quadratic attention scaling and memory bottlenecks as documents grow. * Ultra-Long Document Parsing SOTA: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across both dozens-of-pages benchmarks (e.g., MPDocBench) and extreme hundred-page benchmarks (e.g., MarathonDocBench).
## Inference > Unlimited OCR 2 supports **Transformers** (native, for quick tests) and **SGLang** (recommended for serving). ### Transformers Tested with Python 3.10, `torch==2.13.0`, `transformers==4.52.1`, `huggingface-hub==0.36.0`, `tokenizers==0.21.4`, on an NVIDIA A800-80GB: ```shell pip install torch==2.13.0 torchvision pillow transformers==4.52.1 huggingface-hub==0.36.0 \ tokenizers==0.21.4 addict==2.4.0 einops==0.8.2 easydict==1.13 ``` Load the model once: ```python import torch from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer model_name = "baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2" tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True) model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True, use_safetensors=True, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval().cuda() ``` **Multi-page inference** (`infer_multi`). All pages of a document are parsed in one request, so the model can use cross-page context. Pass the page images in page order: ```python pages = [f"your_doc/page_{i}.jpg" for i in range(1, 8)] text, num_tokens = model.infer_multi(tokenizer, image_files=pages, output_path="output/multi", save_results=True) ``` The prompt is built automatically as `"" * num_pages + "Multi page parsing."`, and each page is encoded as one global view (base mode). The output contains one `` per input page, in the same order as `image_files`. **Single-page inference** (`infer`). A single page is encoded with dynamic tiling (gundam mode) by default: ```python text = model.infer(tokenizer, image_file="your_doc/page_1.jpg", output_path="output/single", save_results=True) ``` ### SGLang Set up the environment (uv-managed virtualenv, Python 3.10) and install the customized SGLang wheel `sglang-0.5.20.dev13+g75b9b06b02-py3-none-any.whl`, plus PyMuPDF for PDF-to-image conversion: ```shell uv venv --python 3.10 source .venv/bin/activate uv pip install wheel/sglang-0.5.20.dev13+g75b9b06b02-py3-none-any.whl uv pip install pymupdf==1.27.2.2 uv pip install fastokens==0.3.2 ``` Start the SGLang server: ```shell # Page-window scheduling for very long documents (the KV tail of the previous window is reused). export SGLANG_UOCR_EANABLE_DOC_LIMIT=1 # 1 = enable, 0 = whole document in one window export SGLANG_UOCR_DOC_GUNDAM_PAGE_WINDOW=10 # pages per window (gundam mode) export SGLANG_UOCR_DOC_BASE_PAGE_WINDOW=10 # pages per window (base mode) export SGLANG_UOCR_MAX_PAGE_TOKENS=20000 # per-page output cap; must be > 0 # Chunk cap for the SAM attention bias. The built-in default (512) allows a single # ~462 MiB allocation and can OOM; 64 is equivalent with a lower peak. export SGLANG_OPT_UOCR_SAM_REL_POS_BIAS_MB=64 # Pass large crop tensors through /dev/shm instead of pickling them into the # tokenizer -> scheduler frame. export SGLANG_UOCR_SHM_WRAP_MODEL_DATA=1 export SGLANG_UOCR_SHM_WRAP_MIN_MB=1 export SGLANG_VLM_CACHE_SIZE_MB=0 # Reduces fragmentation failures on the large contiguous allocations. export PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path baidu/Unlimited-OCR-2 \ --served-model-name Unlimited-OCR-2 \ --chat-template unlimited-ocr \ --tokenizer-backend fastokens \ --tokenizer-worker-num 8 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.7 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --max-prefill-tokens 2048 \ --enable-custom-logit-processor \ --enable-streaming-session \ --allow-auto-truncate \ --disable-radix-cache \ --mm-preprocess-cache-size-mb 0 \ --cuda-graph-backend-decode full --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \ --cuda-graph-backend-prefill full \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-prefill 16384 \ --cuda-graph-bs-prefill 1024 2048 \ --cuda-graph-config '{"prefill": {"backend": "full", "full_prefill_max_req": 64}}' \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 10000 ``` Notes on the knobs that matter for memory: * `--mem-fraction-static` is the share reserved for weights + KV. `0.75` leaves too little headroom at 32+ concurrent requests; `0.7` is stable. * `--max-prefill-tokens` drives a temporary tensor of roughly `[tokens, context/32]`, so memory grows linearly with it: `4096 -> 2048` halves that peak. * The largest `--cuda-graph-bs-prefill` bucket must equal `--max-prefill-tokens`. A smaller one makes oversized batches fall back to eager; a larger one is never used and only wastes capture memory. * `--cuda-graph-config`'s `full_prefill_max_req` is the request-slot count for the full-prefill CUDA graph. The default (8) makes 16/32 concurrency fall back to eager. * A smaller page window lowers peak memory but hurts cross-page merging, since blocks that continue across a window boundary lose their context. To parse a whole document in one window instead (`SGLANG_UOCR_EANABLE_DOC_LIMIT=0`). Send requests to the OpenAI-compatible API: ```python import base64 import json import os import tempfile import fitz import requests from sglang.srt.sampling.custom_logit_processor import DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor server_url = "http://127.0.0.1:10000" NGRAM_PROCESSOR = DeepseekOCRNoRepeatNGramLogitProcessor.to_str() session = requests.Session() session.trust_env = False def pdf_to_images(pdf_path, dpi=300): doc = fitz.open(pdf_path) tmp_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="pdf_ocr_") mat = fitz.Matrix(dpi / 72, dpi / 72) image_paths = [] for i, page in enumerate(doc): image_path = os.path.join(tmp_dir, f"page_{i + 1:04d}.png") page.get_pixmap(matrix=mat).save(image_path) image_paths.append(image_path) doc.close() return image_paths def encode_image(image_path): ext = os.path.splitext(image_path)[1].lower() mime = "image/jpeg" if ext in (".jpg", ".jpeg") else f"image/{ext.lstrip('.')}" with open(image_path, "rb") as f: data = base64.b64encode(f.read()).decode("utf-8") return {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": f"data:{mime};base64,{data}"}} def build_content(image_paths): prompt = "" * len(image_paths) + "Multi page parsing." return [encode_image(path) for path in image_paths] + [{"type": "text", "text": prompt}] def generate(image_paths, crop_mode=True, tokens_per_page=8000): # A wider n-gram window for multi-page documents, as in our evaluation setup. window_size = 1024 if len(image_paths) > 1 else 128 payload = { "model": "Unlimited-OCR-2", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": build_content(image_paths)}], # Must be positive: it is the global output budget for the whole document. "max_tokens": tokens_per_page * len(image_paths), "temperature": 0, "skip_special_tokens": False, "images_config": {"crop_mode": crop_mode}, # True = gundam (tiles), False = base "custom_logit_processor": NGRAM_PROCESSOR, "custom_params": { "ngram_size": 35, "window_size": window_size, "page_token_id": 128827, # marker id (= sparse_attention_config.page_token_id) "eos_token_id": 1, # = eos_token_id in config.json "max_page_tokens": 20000, # per-page output cap, <= 0 disables the page guard }, "stream": True, } response = session.post( f"{server_url}/v1/chat/completions", headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}, data=json.dumps(payload), timeout=6000, stream=True, ) response.raise_for_status() chunks = [] for line in response.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True): if not line or not line.startswith("data:"): continue data = line[len("data:"):].strip() if data == "[DONE]": break event = json.loads(data) choices = event.get("choices") or [] # the final chunk carries usage only if not choices: continue delta = (choices[0].get("delta") or {}).get("content") or "" if delta: print(delta, end="", flush=True) chunks.append(delta) return "".join(chunks) # Multi page: all pages of a document, parsed in one request pages = [f"your_doc/page_{i}.jpg" for i in range(1, 8)] generate(pages) # Single page generate(["your_doc/page_1.jpg"]) # PDF generate(pdf_to_images("your_doc.pdf", dpi=300)) ``` ## Evaluation `infer.py` is the batch client we use for MPDocBench / MarathonDocBench: it sends each document to the SGLang server above as a single request and saves the raw output, which `utils/process_unlimitedOCR2.py` then converts to the evaluation Markdown. ```shell python infer.py --url 127.0.0.1:10000 --benchmark MPDocBench \ --dataset-root /path/to/MPDocBench --all --raw-dir raw --concurrency 4 python utils/process_unlimitedOCR2.py --infer-dir raw --out-dir pred ``` See [utils/README.md](utils/README.md) for the output format, the merging rules and the post-processing details. ## Visualization Unlimited-horizon parsing in action: a full-length book parsed in a single request (replay).
